paper.title_en: High-Dimensional Maximally Entangled OAM States by Joint Pump and Modal-Space Engineering
paper.abstract_en: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) generates correlated photon pairs that inherently exhibit high-dimensional spatial entanglement in orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes. In practice, the resulting two-photon states are typically not maximally entangled due to a highly non-uniform distribution of generated OAM modes. Although pump-beam engineering has emerged as a tool to prepare high-dimensional entangled states, it has usually been restricted to low-dimensional subspaces, i.e., small sets of selected OAM modes for each photon within the full infinite-dimensional two-photon Hilbert space. A general understanding of the requirements for the generation of maximally entangled states (MESs) for any dimensionality $d$ with $d>2$ is lacking. Here, we demonstrate how pump engineering enables the generation of high-dimensional MESs for arbitrary $d$ defined in $d \times d$ subspaces. By identifying the interplay between the spatial pump structure and the choice of OAM subspace, the required pump profile for a target MES is directly determined. Our results reveal that maximal entanglement with OAM requires a careful and nontrivial design of the effective high-dimensional Hilbert subspace.
